# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This is the online version of **Design and Analysis of
Clinical Trials: A ten-week graduate course** by The
rgtlab Curriculum Project.

This book covers the design, conduct, monitoring,
analysis, and reporting of randomized clinical trials. It
is written for first- and second-year graduate students in
biostatistics, epidemiology, and public health, and for
medical students with an interest in research. The core is
structured for a single ten-week academic quarter, one
chapter per week, each roughly two hours of lecture and
four to six hours of assigned work. Eighteen further
chapters treat advanced topics in depth, for readers who
continue past the quarter.

The organizing claim of the book is straightforward. A
trial is an experiment whose design decisions are made
once, in advance, under uncertainty. Once the first patient
is randomized, none of those decisions can be revised.
Everything the book teaches follows from that constraint.
We see why the estimand must be specified before the
sample size, why the randomization procedure dictates the
analysis model, and why interim looks must be priced into
the type I error before the first look is taken. Lastly,
we see why a pre-specified analysis of imperfect data is
worth more than a perfect analysis chosen after the data
are already in hand.

The ten weeks are:

1. The trial as an experiment: history, ethics, regulation.
2. The protocol, the estimand, and the endpoint.
3. Randomization and allocation concealment.
4. Blinding, bias, and trial conduct.
5. Sample size and power.
6. Phase I: dose-finding designs.
7. Phase II: screening designs.
8. Phase III: the primary analysis.
9. Interim monitoring, group-sequential, and adaptive designs.
10. Missing data, sensitivity analysis, and reporting.

The book sits in the rgtlab graduate sequence:

- [*R for Biostatistics: A One-Week Boot Camp*](https://r-bootcamp.rgtlab.org),
  pre-program preparation in the R language.
- [*Biostatistics Practicum*](https://practicum.rgtlab.org),
  workflow and reproducibility infrastructure.
- [*Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai.rgtlab.org),
  introductory methods and computing.
- [*Advanced Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai-advanced.rgtlab.org),
  advanced numerical and Bayesian computation.
- [*Applied Statistical Methods for Health Sciences Research*](https://applied-methods.rgtlab.org),
  the applied-methods axis, whose two clinical-trial
  chapters this volume expands into a full course.
- [*Applied Generative AI for Health Sciences Research*](https://applied-genai.rgtlab.org),
  generative AI as the orthogonal axis.
- *Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials* (this volume),
  the trials axis.

See the [Preface](preface.qmd) for motivation and the
[Conventions](conventions.qmd) page for visual cues.
